# 4 Ezra Chapter 3 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 4 Ezra Chapter 3 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 3:8 — register and tone of opening formula in Latin

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "hyper-literal compound rendering" | Preserves Latin conjunction and syntax literally |
| LOGOS | "formal English equivalent" | Formal rendering preserving structure in natural English |
| PNEUMA | "dynamic modern English paraphrase" | Natural English; reduces repetitive source-language formulae |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The Latin formula is a standard narrative connector best preserved formally without EMET's hyphenation or PNEUMA's compression.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Minor stylistic divergence.

---

## 3:15 — theological key term — Latin technical vocabulary

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "transliterated or hyper-literal term" | Preserves the Latin term's full semantic range |
| LOGOS | "standard scholarly English equivalent" | Recognized translation in academic literature |
| PNEUMA | "functional modern paraphrase" | Accessible to readers without ancient language background |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The technical term carries theological weight that PNEUMA's paraphrase dilutes, while EMET's transliteration is inaccessible to English readers.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Theologically significant terminology.

---

## 3:22 — verbal aspect: Latin verb form rendered differently

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "morphologically literal rendering" | Preserves the Latin verbal stem and aspect |
| LOGOS | "contextually appropriate English tense" | English tense best representing the narrative function |
| PNEUMA | "vivid present-tense rendering for immediacy" | Historic present creates narrative tension for modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The verbal aspect in context indicates completed action; PNEUMA's historic present creates false immediacy, while EMET's morphological literalism reads awkwardly in English.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Aspectual — narrative register matters.

---

## 3:29 — divine epithet or title — translation vs. preservation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "transliterated divine title" | Preserves the source-language title as a proper name |
| LOGOS | "translated divine title with capitalization" | Standard rendering in English translations; treats it as a title |
| PNEUMA | "descriptive paraphrase of the divine attribute" | Makes the meaning of the title transparent to the reader |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. Divine titles carry both referential and theological weight. The LOGOS approach preserves the title structure while making it English-accessible, unlike EMET (opaque) or PNEUMA (loses the title form).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Theologically significant — divine naming conventions.

---
